# Appendix D — Architecture Assurance Checklist

**Intent and decisions**

☐  Business outcome, scope and constraints are explicit.

☐  Priority quality attributes have measurable scenarios.

☐  Alternatives, risks and ADRs are recorded with owners.

**Design**

☐  Context and container views and interface contracts have owners.

☐  Platform dependencies — capability contracts, the responsibility split and the isolation model — are recorded (17.3.1, 17.5.2, 17.6.1).

☐  Data ownership, classification and a retention schedule (including files, logs and backups) are defined.

☐  Audit trails and data change history meet regulatory and contractual requirements.

☐  Threats are modeled and controls mapped to tests.

☐  Privacy decisions — minimization, retention, transfers, data-subject requests and a DPIA where required — are recorded (13.9).

☐  Authentication, SSO and authorization designs are reviewed; privileged access is controlled.

☐  The security test strategy (SAST, SCA, authenticated DAST, penetration test) and vulnerability remediation objectives are defined.

**Evidence and operations**

☐  Failure scenarios, RTO/RPO and capacity assumptions are tested; BCP and DRP are current.

☐  A cloud well-architected review is completed, and critical suppliers are assessed.

☐  Deployment, rollback and observability are operationally ready.

☐  A test strategy covers priority quality scenarios, contract tests and quality gates.

☐  The change approval model for the solution is agreed and produces auditable evidence.

☐  Governance exceptions have owners, expiry dates and remediation plans.

☐  Operational ownership and runbooks are accepted by the operating team.

**Recording the assessment**

The checklist states what to review; record the outcome separately so that the checklist stays reusable. For each item, capture:

| Field | Values or content |
| :--- | :--- |
| Applicability | Applicable or Not applicable, with the reason when not applicable |
| Status | Pass, Partial, Fail or Not assessed |
| Evidence | Reference to the artifact, test result or record that supports the status |
| Finding and remediation | What is missing, the remediation owner and the due date |
| Reviewer and date | Who assessed the item and when |

: Recording the checklist assessment

A Partial or Fail status without an owner and a date is a risk accepted by default; route it to the accountable owner (4.5).
